text:
maria: Heads-up: we're aiming to publish the release announcement tomorrow 10:00am PT. Need: final changelog blurb, canonical docs link, a 1-sentence benchmark callout for the blog, webinar scheduling confirmation, and the inbound lead routing plan. Can eng confirm canary cadence and any user-facing caveats?

 kevin: Canary plan looks good from infra side. Proposal: 5% at T+5m, 25% at T+30m, 75% at T+2h, full at T+6h if error_rate & latency within thresholds. We'll instrument a short-lived regression alarm for 15m windows. Changelog draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/changelog/pull/522.

 rittika: Docs staging URL is https://docs.redwood.ai/staging/release-1.2.0; examples updated but need a quick sanity check on the code sample that shows the new request-coalescing param. @kevin can you run the sample in staging?

 kevin: Running now. Quick note: request_coalesce=true default changes latency profile for small payloads; we'll add a footnote in the docs. Sample output looks good.

 deploy-bot: Canary start scheduled by @kevin at 2024-05-14T17:00:00Z. Observability hooks: latency_p95, cpu_util, error_rate. Auto-rollback enabled.

 noah: Marketing bench blurb candidate: "Request coalescing reduced median latency by ~15% on chat workloads and lowered token cost by ~8% in our internal tests." Short and citation-free. Thoughts?

 claire: That reads fine. Can we include the test workload name (chat-mix-v3) in the tech notes but not in the main blog? Also need a small image: p95 before/after graph. Who can export?

 hari: I can pull the graph from bench dashboard and export a PNG by EOD. Which metrics should we show? p95 and cost-per-token.

 maria: Perfect. For inbound routing: we'll tag all release landing forms with campaign=may_release_1_2 and source=blog. HubSpot workflow will route to SDR queue A and create SFDC campaign. @rittika can you confirm webhook endpoint?

 rittika: Webhook endpoint validated. Payload includes campaign, utm_source, email, company. HubSpot flow: https://internal.redwood/hubspot/workflows/rel-1-2.

 kevin: Small deployment note to include in the public changelog: "Enabled request coalescing for small-payload traffic, improved cold-start KV initialization reducing first-token latency, and added a controlled canary with auto-rollback on elevated error rates."

 noah: Webinar: confirmed Thu 11am ET (Thu 8am PT). I'll send calendar invites and include a registration CTA on the blog. Who's presenting?

 claire: Product will present; engineering (kevin) will do a short live demo. We should avoid deep infra slides; focus on user impact and cost/latency numbers.

 kevin: I'll prepare a single slide showing before/after p95 + a high-level diagram of request coalescing.

 maria: Last asks: kevin paste final changelog sentence in this thread; rittika give final docs permalink; hari drop the bench PNG link. If all green, I'll hit publish 10:00am PT tomorrow.

 kevin: Changelog sentence: "Enabled request coalescing for small-payload traffic, improved KV initialization to reduce cold-start latency, and added a staged canary with auto-rollback on elevated error rates."

 rittika: Docs canonical link: https://docs.redwood.ai/release/1.2.0 — examples verified.

 hari: Bench image uploaded: https://internal.redwood/assets/rel-1-2/p95-cost-compare.png

 deploy-bot: Canary started at 2024-05-14T17:00:00Z. Monitoring: latency_p95=310ms (ok), error_rate=0.08% (ok).

 maria: Locking announce for 10:00am PT. We'll include the short bench blurb, changelog sentence, docs link, webinar CTA (Thu 11am ET), and HubSpot routing tag. Thanks everyone, publishing tomorrow unless a blocker appears. :rocket:
